subject: Proposal: Dedicated capacity uplift + EU/APAC failover plan — renewal conversation
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie@nebula-analytics.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated expansion + multi-region failover for Nebula Analytics (renewal)

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the hosted demo last month. As we approach our contract renewal (2027-01-15), the platform team here at Nebula has put together a formal request to expand our dedicated capacity and codify multi-region failover. High level: we want to add reserved pools in EU and APAC to reduce p95 latency for EU customers and provide deterministic failover from our US pool.

Key asks from our side:
- Reserved capacity: additional capacity equivalent to ~60 A100-class GPUs total (we've split this as 30 EU, 30 APAC as a starting point).
- Throughput/latency: target p95 generation latency under 80ms for EU (regional traffic) and under 140ms for APAC; global failover should not increase p95 by more than 30–40ms.
- Throughput guarantee: sustained aggregate token throughput of ~100k tokens/sec across their active pools during business hours, with short bursts above that.
- Term changes: prefer a 12-month committed term for the uplift tied to a renewal amendment and a 10–15% price concession vs on-demand if we commit to the uplift.
- Operational: require dedicated monitoring dashboards, cross-region routing policy, and a documented runbook for cross-region failover and cache warming.

Attached is our internal renewal request doc and a simple latency histogram from our test runs. Can you confirm feasibility and provide a ballpark price and SLA language we can circulate with our procurement team? We can set a technical sync early next week — Tom (cc'd) will join for capacity profiling.

Thanks,
Sophie Lang
Director, ML Platform
Nebula Analytics

Attachments:
- Nebula_Renewal_Request_v2.pdf (pdf stub)
- latency_histogram.csv (csv stub)

Sophie — thanks for sending this through and for the clear asks. We're excited to continue supporting Nebula and to explore a multi-region reserved footprint.

Quick notes and next steps from our side:
- Feasibility: short answer — yes, adding regional reserved pools is something we can do. Marcus (cc) will provide an initial capacity/latency estimate and any tradeoffs (model variants, quantization, batching).
- SLA & pricing: we'll produce a draft amendment with throughput targets and a proposed price band. Procurement usually needs a 2–3 week turnaround for final amendment redlines.
- Runbook & observability: Redwood Console can expose per-route latency/cost dashboards and we can provide a runbook for failover + KV cache pre-warm strategies.

Can we plan a 30-minute technical sync on Wed 12:00–12:30 PT or Thu 10:00–10:30 PT? Please confirm which works for your team. I will circulate an internal summary after the sync and include preliminary pricing ranges.

Forwarding for internal alignment — Laura/Marcus/Neha: see Sophie’s asks above. Marcus — can you include a short note on GPU counts and whether we should propose a mixed pool (e.g., some higher-memory nodes for large-context models)? Neha — recommend we include the standard 30-day credit clause and discuss discount structure.

Best,

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 07:02:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: Dedicated expansion + multi-region failover for Nebula Analytics (renewal)

Olga / team — quick capacity and price-first-draft for the sync. Notes below are internal and meant to be converted into a clean customer-facing proposal after we confirm the peak token profile.

Summary proposal (internal):
- Proposed reserved capacity: EU pool = 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs; APAC pool = 28 x A100-equivalent GPUs. That gives headroom for the stated sustained throughput (~100k tokens/s) with room for KV cache warming/cold starts.
- Model considerations: if Nebula is using larger context Llama-3-class models we should reserve ~10% of the nodes with larger vRAM (or advise quantized variants to reduce memory).
- Throughput SLA: propose a contractual throughput target of 95k–110k tokens/sec across regional pools (measured per 5-minute window), with credits if sustained falls below target for longer than a 2-hour window.
- Latency assumptions: with the proposed capacity and our routing policy we expect EU p95s in the 60–85ms range and APAC p95s in the 110–150ms range depending on model variant. Cross-region failover should add ~20–40ms median overhead for traffic that needs to cross the ocean; recommend customers plan for up to 50ms impact during warm-up.
- Billing & discounting: recommend offering a 20% uplift commitment tier (customer commits to 20% more than current baseline) and give a 10% committed-use discount; for higher commitments (>=40% uplift) consider 18% discount + extended payment terms.

Operational asks for proposal doc:
- Dedicated dashboards by region, token-level cost breakout, alerting thresholds, and a failover runbook with steps for cache pre-warm and traffic re-route.
- 72-hour capacity provisioning window for additional burst beyond reserved capacity (subject to availability).

Attachments: capacity_planning_estimate.xlsx (internal stub).

I’ll attach a simple spreadsheet with node counts and rough cost multipliers for the meeting. If legal wants to push a stricter SLA we should include clear credit calculations.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sophie / Tom — thanks for the clarity and for giving us time to align internally. Quick recap and next steps so everything is explicit before we meet: 

Recap (provisional):
- Redwood can provision regional reserved pools for EU and APAC. Internal draft suggests ~32 GPUs EU / ~28 GPUs APAC (final numbers dependent on model/context).
- Target throughput SLA: 95k–110k tokens/sec (measured per 5-minute window).
- Latency expectations: EU p95 ~60–85ms; APAC p95 ~110–150ms. Failover-induced overhead estimated at ~20–40ms, plan for up to 50ms during cache warm-up.
- Pricing guidance: provisional committed-use discount range 10% (base uplift) — 18% (larger uplift tiers). Final pricing will be in the term amendment.
- Operational deliverables: per-region dashboards, runbook for failover and cache pre-warm, and a 72-hour burst provisioning SLA for temporary capacity spikes.

Requested from Nebula before the sync:
- A short peak token profile (CSV) showing per-hour token volume for a representative week.
- Confirmation of model families and typical context length (so Marcus can finalize node mix).
- Procurement contact for DocuSign/send-back of an amendment when ready.

Proposed times for a 30-minute technical sync (I’ll send calendar invites once you confirm): Wed 12:00–12:30 PT or Thu 10:00–10:30 PT next week.

If you want a written draft amendment before the call, we can prepare one but it will be provisional until we lock the technical details. I’ll also create a short one-page summary for procurement and drop it into the HubSpot deal.
